title: Sensitization is harder to break than habituation in pathway models

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Sensitization is harder to break than habituation in pathway models

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In ODE pathway models, sensitization could be broken by stimulating a third node in only 8 of 27 sensitizing models, mostly for fewer than 5% of node pairs, so breaking sensitization is less likely than breaking habituation and therapies may need other avenues of intervention.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.8. Making and Breaking Sensitization

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Overall, we conclude that while sensitization is prevalent in biological models, the breaking of sensitization is less likely than in habituation, and therefore therapeutic models may need to pursue other avenues of intervention.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.8. Making and Breaking Sensitization”. Scope: 27 sensitizing ODE pathway models from BioModels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-18: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.89

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both sides of the comparison are defined in the same finite model suite with explicit thresholds. Existing models are sufficient to check the stated simulation result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Search all third-node interventions in sensitizing models and compare the fraction of models and pairs broken with the corresponding habituation results. The reported 8-of-27 and less-than-5% pattern are direct criteria.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The intervention search is limited to modeled node stimulation.

Therapeutic feasibility is not represented.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.86
data existence: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.97

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both breaking assays use an explicit ratio rule and a third-node search, and the code covers sensitization as well as pharmacoresistance. Re-running them yields the 8-of-27 count and the pair-fraction comparison directly. The remark about therapies needing other avenues is an interpretation of that same rate difference.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On each sensitizing model, apply the third-node breaking protocol and record whether the 1.5-fold rise is abolished, and for what fraction of pairs. Breaks confined to 8 of 27 models and mostly under 5 percent of pairs, at a lower rate than habituation breaking, would confirm the claim; breaks in most models or in large pair fractions would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: The comparison with habituation uses the same style of search, but the pair denominators differ across models.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.74
data adequacy: 0.8
data existence: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.9
